transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-07-08 10:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM), Maya (AstraHealth CTO), Liam (AstraHealth SRE), Nora (AstraHealth ML Eng), Samir (AstraHealth Security)
Shared artifacts: benchmark spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.app/sheets/astra-bench-0708), network diagram draft, SOC2 summary PDF

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call - can you all hear me?
[00:12] Maya: yes loud and clear, thanks Alex. quick time check we have about 45, is that right?
[00:18] Alex: yep 45 minutes, lot to go through - Priya and I will walk through the latest benchmark slide and the live numbers vs the baseline provider you shared.
[00:28] Priya: cool, i'll start with the high level. we ran the same 1k synthetic prompts you provided with your baseline config and then our recommended config: prefix caching on, batch target 32, dynamic KV reuse and int8 quantized weights for the smaller model.
[00:45] Liam: quick Q - when you say int8, is that post-training quantization you do in service or a compiled path?
[00:51] Priya: it's a quantized execution path in our runtime, compiled ahead of time during model onboarding; it's not altering your upstream model artifact, it's a runtime kernel path so your original FP16 remains available if you want it.
[01:05] Nora: ok that matters for quality checks - did you measure any drop in rouge scores or generation quality?
[01:10] Priya: we ran the same eval set, quality delta was within noise for this workload - mean F1 change ~0.6% and you can see per-prompt examples in the sheet. we flagged 12 prompts that need manual review.
[01:22] Alex: on latency numbers: baseline provider P95 was ~420ms, median ~120ms for single token streaming. Redwood in hosted default config P95 = 280ms, median ~90ms. With recommended batching and prefix cache the P95 drops to ~220ms and throughput jumps from 120 rps to about 220 rps on the same instance class.
[01:46] Maya: those are nice gains - can you call out cost delta? baseline cost per 1M tokens was in sheet under col D.
[01:52] Alex: yes cost is about 28% lower for Redwood in this config because the KV caching and batching reduce repeat generation work. we've annotated cost-per-token and unit economics in the spreadsheet.
[02:05] Liam: curious about variability - your P95 numbers look better but baseline had lower median in some runs previously. what's the jitter like over a 1 hour run?
[02:15] Priya: good question. we did a 1-hour sustained run. Redwood 95th stayed stable +/- 10ms across windows; baseline had occasional spikes up to 700ms during GC or noisy neighbor events in their managed offering. we included time-series graphs.
[02:31] Jordan: worth calling out the dedicated option - if Astra goes dedicated, the variability goes down further and throughput increases but cost model changes to reserved capacity.
[02:40] Maya: we are sensitive to cost but require predictability for SLAs. can you sketch the dedicated throughput numbers?
[02:46] Priya: on a single dedicated GPU pod sized for this model we measured sustained 320 rps with P95 at ~180ms using our batching and cache; that's with quantized int8 exec. If you want FP16 the P95 is ~210ms and rps is ~280.
[02:59] Samir: security question - you mentioned KV cache, anything stored outside ephemeral GPU memory? we need to confirm no persistent customer data is cached off-host.
[03:08] Priya: KV cache is in-memory on the inference node and ephemeral; cached entries are not written to disk. for private deployments we can control network egress and KMS, and we support customer-managed keys for auditability.
[03:20] Samir: great, please add that to the security doc you send.
[03:24] Alex: will do. next, on tuning knobs - we recommended bumping batch target to 32 for this workload because prompt length distribution is short, so aggregation improves throughput without hurting latency. we also suggested auto-burst policy for traffic spikes.
[03:39] Nora: is batching client-side or server-side? we prefer server-side so we don't change client retry semantics.
[03:44] Priya: server-side batching in the runtime; your clients keep the same API. we expose rate hints and you can set max latency SLO to avoid head-of-line waits.
[03:55] Liam: what about model fallbacks? if dedicated is saturated will you route to hosted?
[03:59] Alex: yes we can set smart routing policies - route by latency tier, cost tier, region, or model variant. automatic fallback to compatible variant is possible with canary rules.
[04:09] Maya: going back to the sheet - i noticed one of your rows shows Redwood P99 higher than baseline. why would that be?
[04:16] Priya: P99 captures tail noise, in our run one pod had an out-of-band scheduling event during collection that inflated a few samples. when we re-ran with pod pinning it matched the P95 trends. we included the rerun tab.
[04:28] Alex: to be practical, we recommend looking at P95 for SLA planning and P99 for further tail mitigation work if you need 99.9% uptime latency.
[04:36] Maya: understood. on quality tradeoffs - if we push more aggressive quantization like int4 will that materially change behavior?
[04:44] Priya: int4 will reduce inference cost but we observed cases where answer fidelity dropped on abstractive tasks; we can run a targeted eval set to surface where int4 fails. recommended path: start int8, evaluate, then selectively int4 for non-critical routes.
[04:58] Nora: would that be per-route model variant?
[05:01] Priya: yes you can pin routes to model variants and use routing policy to decide fallbacks.
[05:06] Liam: ops question - how do we monitor token-level costs and attribution?
[05:10] Jordan: Console provides token-level cost breakdowns, per-route dashboards, traces, and exported CSVs for billing reconciliation. we'll share a screenshot and export sample.
[05:19] Maya: okay next - we want to run a 10k sample on our dev data to sanity-check quality and latency under our prompt distribution. what's the best way to submit that test?
[05:27] Alex: upload a csv to the secure bucket link in the sheet or provide it via s3 with presigned url; we'll ingest and run the job. expect results in 48 hours for a 10k job.
[05:36] Maya: perfect.
[05:39] Samir: also you'll send SOC2 and network diagram?
[05:42] Alex: yes we'll send SOC2 summary and the draft network architecture doc to Samir by Friday.
[05:48] Priya: just one more technical detail - we saw larger gains when enabling prefix-level KV reuse for streaming chat use cases; because your prompts often share context, cache hit rates were ~35% which drove a lot of the throughput wins.
[06:02] Nora: that cache hit assumes similar prefix tokens - does the cache invalidate on user session boundaries?
[06:07] Priya: yes caches are keyed by session id and prompt prefix rules; you can configure TTLs.
[06:14] Liam: any surprise blocker from our infra side? egress rules?
[06:18] Alex: for hosted we need outbound to our control plane for telemetry, but for Private/VPC we can operate with a control plane proxy. we'll document the minimal ports.
[06:27] Maya: what's the timeline if we wanted to try dedicated pilot?
[06:31] Jordan: typical pilot is 4 weeks: week 1 onboarding + benchmark, week 2 run customer dataset and tuning, week 3 integrate SSO/KMS and run longer stability test, week 4 finalize configs and pricing.
[06:45] Maya: ok good.
[06:48] Liam: on pricing, can you share a ballpark for dedicated reserved pod vs hosted per-token at the numbers in the sheet?
[06:56] Alex: rough ballpark in the sheet - dedicated reserved commit reduces per-token unit cost by ~30% vs peak hosted for sustained throughput. we'll include the breakdown in the updated sheet.
[07:08] Samir: last security note - we need to confirm key rotation policy and where audit logs live.
[07:14] Alex: logs can be pushed to your Splunk or S3 with object-level encryption and include per-request metadata. key rotation is via KMS integration and we support customer-managed keys.
[07:26] Maya: great, let's capture the blockers: 1) run 10k dev job, 2) share SOC2 + network diagram, 3) send recommended configs and cost breakout - is that fair?
[07:36] Alex: yes and we'll schedule the dedicated scoping call for week of 7/20 pending your infra availability.
[07:42] Priya: i'll also add a small set of flagged prompts where quality changed, so Nora can triage.
[07:49] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll reconvene after the 10k run.
[07:55] Alex: thanks, meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcript has occasional speaker overlap and auto-transcription errors (names sometimes misspelled). benchmark spreadsheet contains raw samples, time-series graphs, and rerun tab.
